fixes.explanation: That's it, baker. Mark says the large crowd came to Him "…when they heard what great things He was doing." (Mark 3:8) Word got around, and I bet nobody needed a group chat to spread it. People came from Galilee, Judea, Jerusalem and more.
Not laws, friend. The text says the crowd came "…when they heard what great things He was doing." (Mark 3:8) The reason Mark gives is what He was doing, and he doesn't mention new laws here.
Thanking Him sounds lovely, but that's not the word Mark uses. The text says all who had diseases were "…pressing forward to touch Him." (Mark 3:10) Touch is the word the verse gives.

Close, friend, since a large crowd did go along with Him. (Mark 3:7) But this verse says those who had diseases were "…pressing forward to touch Him." (Mark 3:10) Touch is the word that fits the blank.
Nope, friend. The spirits don't call Jesus Elijah. They fell down before Him and cried out, "You are the Son of God!" (Mark 3:11) They named Him correctly.
That's not what they said, baker. The unclean spirits fell down and cried out, "You are the Son of God!" (Mark 3:11) They didn't mix Him up with anybody.
Not quite, baker. The text says the opposite. Jesus "…warned them sternly not to make Him known." (Mark 3:12) So He didn't want them making Him known, and He was stern about it.

False is right, baker. Mark says Jesus "…warned them sternly not to make Him known." (Mark 3:12) The spirits cried out who He was, but He warned them sternly. I think that's a pretty serious tone, so I'd listen.

Not volunteers, friend. Jesus "…called for those He wanted, and they came to Him." (Mark 3:13) Mark puts the wanting on Jesus' side. I know what it's like to be called when I didn't see it coming. An angel called me out of a junk drawer.
Preach is right, baker. Jesus appointed the twelve "…to be sent out to preach…" (Mark 3:14) Being sent out to preach is part of why He appointed them, along with being with Him.
Build is a fine word, baker, but it's not in this passage. Jesus appointed them "…to be sent out to preach…" (Mark 3:14) Hammers and blueprints aren't in that verse.

Storms are a good guess, since Jesus does calm the wind and sea later in Mark. (Mark 4:39) But in this passage the authority is "…to drive out demons." (Mark 3:15) That's the exact word. Weather isn't on this list.

I see why you'd go there, baker, since Jesus withdrew to the sea earlier in this passage. (Mark 3:7) But the naming happens with the twelve, and Mark says Boanerges means "Sons of Thunder…" (Mark 3:17) The name is all about thunder.
